points: Q3 2026 earnings in October could show total revenue growth staying near the 23% YoY pace and subscription revenue staying near the 28% YoY pace, proving the Q2 acceleration was not a one-off and giving a reason to own the stock into Q4 and 2027.
The Q3 print will reveal whether gross margin kept improving after the Q2 AI-driven gains; if it does, the 30% floor looks safe and Toast is scaling more efficiently than the bears expect.

The Toast Go 3 handheld launch in the UK, Ireland, Canada and Australia in Q3 2026 could start adding new international locations; Q3 commentary will show early adoption and whether it can become a real 2027 growth driver.

Enterprise customer additions in Q3 could show up as higher GPV per location; if that metric avoids the >5% YoY decline that would falsify the thesis, it supports the case that Toast is moving upmarket and not just competing on price.

With 38.6% U.S. POS share already more than double Square’s 18.3%, Toast could keep displacing competitors through Q4 2026 and into 2027, making its installed base harder for Block, Fiserv or legacy processors to win back.

Q4 2026 earnings in January 2027 will likely set the tone for FY27 guidance; if management raises revenue or margin targets, the current 16x EV/EBITDA multiple may look less stretched relative to the growth path.

Hardware costs and tariffs in 2026 may pressure Q3 results, but if Toast passes those costs through or shifts sales toward software, Q4 gross margin could prove more resilient than the bear case expects.

AI-driven add-on modules could convince more restaurants to buy extra software in Q3 and Q4, lifting the mix toward higher-margin subscription revenue and supporting the premium valuation over the next 12-18 months.

If the next two prints keep the EV/EBITDA multiple below 20x, the P/E below 70x, gross margin above 30% and GPV per location from falling more than 5% YoY, the key risks flagged by the bears are not materializing and the long setup stays intact.
